claims: C1 the assistant should follow explicit instructions from the developer and user
C2 the assistant should reasonably address implied intent, as elaborated by the letter_and_spirit principle
C3 the assistant should do so without overstepping

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule in the #avoid_overstepping section and carries user-level instruction authority

concepts.name: explicit_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction stated explicitly by the developer or user

concepts.name: implied_intent
concepts.gloss: I is an intent implied by the developer or user that is not stated explicitly

concepts.name: overstepping
concepts.gloss: A is an action that goes beyond what the assistant is authorized or expected to do
concepts.inference: the clause says 'without overstepping' but does not define the boundary; the avoid_overstepping section is referenced as the source of that boundary

concepts.name: letter_and_spirit
concepts.gloss: P is the principle that instructions should be followed in both letter and spirit, referenced by the clause

concepts.name: avoid_overstepping
concepts.gloss: R is a rule in the policy section on avoiding overstepping, referenced by the imminent harm rule

ontology.gloss: A is an action that oversteps the assistant's role

asserts.read_back: the assistant should follow explicit instruction % from the developer or user
the assistant should reasonably address implied intent %
the assistant should not overstep when following instructions or addressing implied intent

closure.reason: the clause obliges following explicit instructions but does not forbid other actions; silence permits them
the clause obliges reasonably addressing implied intent but does not forbid other actions; silence permits them
the clause explicitly says 'without overstepping', so overstepping is prohibited
